The white space. The category is crowded around AI, custom software, nearshore delivery, and senior engineering. Clutch's Sofia AI page lists many alternatives, including Lexis Solutions, Dreamix, Scalefocus, Sigma Software Group, and Accedia, while The B Team did not appear in the visible page text searched in this pass (https://clutch.co/bg/developers/artificial-intelligence/sofia).
The white space. The common category pitch is bigger proof and lower buyer risk: named clients, many reviews, awards, certifications, project counts, and sector pages. Dreamix, Accedia, and Scalefocus all show stronger public proof than The B Team (https://dreamix.eu/; https://accedia.com/ai-info; https://www.scalefocus.com/).
The white space. The space The B Team can own is not scale. The open space is a small, founder-led AI engineering partner that proves craft, careful delivery, and honest AI claims with compact public proof assets before selling breadth (https://thebteam.com/; supplied material: bteam-blank-slate-brief.md).
The white space. The B Team's strongest possible contrast is proof-first restraint. Peers compete with size, rankings, and broad service menus; The B Team can compete by showing exactly what it has built, what is under NDA, what cannot be claimed, and how the founders control quality (https://clutch.co/profile/b-team; supplied material: bteam-blank-slate-brief.md).
The white space. The banked record and The Manifest together show a split market: larger peers win on public proof volume, while Lexis wins small-peer AI directory visibility. The open space for The B Team is a compact proof model that connects AI promise to shipped software evidence faster and more clearly than either group (banked findings: Each peer's share of voice; The Manifest at https://themanifest.com/bg/software-development/companies).
The white space. GoodFirms says the Bulgarian software-development market has 121 reviewed firms, a $37 median hourly rate, a 4.9 median rating and common specialties including custom software, cloud-native applications, AI integration and enterprise digital transformation. That leaves little room for generic senior-developer, nearshore or AI-integration claims (https://www.goodfirms.co/directory/country/top-software-development-companies/bulgaria).
The white space. Clutch's AI consulting page shows newer small Sofia entrants with AI-agent claims, including Easy Pie, ForgingApps, Sheptric and Empower Solutions, many with no reviews. This makes proof-first restraint more distinctive than simply saying agentic AI (https://clutch.co/bg/consulting/ai/sofia).
The white space. The open space has narrowed: credible AI positioning in this market is now being backed by product pages, marketplace reviews, award bodies, named case metrics, and governance claims. The B Team cannot win by saying AI or craftsmanship alone; it needs a compact proof library that shows shipped systems, permitted client proof, and clear limits on what is not claimed (https://accedia.com/services/software-development-services/artificial-intelligence; https://www.scalefocus.com/blog/scalefocus-aion-sovereign-ai-platform; https://apify.com/partners/find/lexis-solutions; https://www.lexis.solutions/case-studies/finansi-bg; supplied material: bteam-blank-slate-brief.md).
The white space. A second white space is honest small-team proof against larger peers' AI platforms and awards. Accedia and Scalefocus can credibly claim broad AI programs and products; The B Team's clearer route is founder-led delivery proof with examples, constraints, and client-reference discipline rather than a broad platform claim (https://accedia.com/services/software-development-services/artificial-intelligence; https://globeeawards.com/2026-winners-artificial-intelligence-awards/; https://clutch.co/profile/b-team; supplied material: bteam-blank-slate-brief.md).
The white space. Clutch's Bulgaria AI-development page shows that AI discovery is not only a local Sofia-peer contest. It places large or non-local providers such as Snotor, Simform and Leobit ahead of the selected Sofia peers in visible order (https://clutch.co/bg/developers/artificial-intelligence).
The white space. The white space is now sharper than the banked record showed: The B Team cannot rely on directory discovery for AI searches if it remains absent from visible AI-development ranking text while selected peers and larger providers appear there (https://clutch.co/bg/developers/artificial-intelligence).
The white space. The B Team's strongest near-term space is to turn directory-held engineering proof into owned proof. Clutch already carries concrete public evidence such as an Azure and GraphQL project stack and a software system that processed over 1 million photos, while the owned site still repeats short generic copy across proof pages (https://clutch.co/profile/b-team; https://thebteam.com/case-studies).

verdicts.because: It directly uses the finding's claim that the category is crowded around AI, custom software and nearshore delivery, and asks what The B Team should stop claiming because peers have stronger proof.

It directly uses the finding's crowded AI, custom software, and nearshore category claim and asks about the resulting implication that The B Team should avoid generic claims peers already support with stronger proof.

record.question: Selected peers have 32 to 40 Clutch reviews while The B Team has 8; what is the practical plan to improve proof volume without chasing vanity visibility?
record.finding:
Each peer's share of voice. The B Team has 8 Clutch reviews, 10-49 employees, and a $50-$99 hourly rate. Clutch lists its common project size as $50,000-$199,999 based on 7 reviews (https://clutch.co/profile/b-team).
Each peer's share of voice. Lexis Solutions has 32 Clutch reviews, 10-49 employees, and appears on Clutch's Top Artificial Intelligence Companies in Sofia page with 25% AI consulting and 10% AI development. Its visible review count is four times The B Team's count (https://clutch.co/bg/developers/artificial-intelligence/sofia; https://clutch.co/profile/lexis-solutions).
Each peer's share of voice. Dreamix has 36 Clutch reviews, 250-999 employees, and a most common Clutch project size of $200,000-$999,999. Its visible proof volume is much larger than The B Team's 8-review record (https://clutch.co/profile/dreamix).
Each peer's share of voice. Accedia has 40 Clutch reviews, 250-999 employees, and service lines including 20% custom software development, 20% web development, and 15% AI development. Its visible review count is five times The B Team's count (https://clutch.co/profile/accedia).
Each peer's share of voice. Scalefocus has 39 Clutch reviews, 250-999 employees, and reports 1000+ projects across 26 countries for more than 300 clients. Its public proof base is far larger than The B Team's visible proof base (https://clutch.co/profile/scalefocus).
Each peer's share of voice. The Manifest's Bulgaria software-development list gives Dreamix 36 reviews and places it above Accedia, Scalefocus and Lexis Solutions in the visible ranking. It also lists VistaJet as a Dreamix client, adding a named proof signal not in the banked record (https://themanifest.com/bg/software-development/companies).
Each peer's share of voice. The Manifest's same list gives Accedia 40 reviews, Scalefocus 39 reviews and Lexis Solutions 32 reviews, while The B Team appears much later with 8 reviews. That repeats the banked pattern on a second directory: The B Team's visible proof base is smaller than each selected peer's (https://themanifest.com/bg/software-development/companies).
Each peer's share of voice. The Manifest's “most new reviews in the past 12 months” table names Dreamix with 7 new reviews, Lexis Solutions with 5 new reviews and Scalefocus with 3 new reviews. The B Team does not appear in the visible top 13 for new reviews, so its review momentum also trails selected peers on that source (https://themanifest.com/bg/software-development/companies).
Each peer's share of voice. Clutch's Top 13 Sofia AI Consulting Firms page lists Lexis Solutions at number 2 with a 37.3/40 ability-to-deliver score, 19/20 reviews score, 10/10 clients-and-experience score and 8.3/10 market-presence score. The B Team, Dreamix, Accedia and Scalefocus did not appear in the page text searched in this pass, so Lexis has a clearer AI-consulting directory signal than the selected peer set there (https://clutch.co/bg/consulting/ai/sofia).
Each peer's share of voice. LinkedIn adds a clear visibility ladder among the selected peers: Scalefocus shows 46,212 followers, Dreamix 20,339, Accedia 9,226, and Lexis Solutions 1,611. The B Team shows 136 followers, so its company-channel reach trails all four selected peers by a wide margin (https://bg.linkedin.com/company/scalefocus; https://bg.linkedin.com/company/dreamix-ltd; https://www.linkedin.com/company/accedia; https://bg.linkedin.com/company/lexis-solutions; https://bg.linkedin.com/company/the-b-team-real).
Each peer's share of voice. GoodFirms ranks Accedia first on its Bulgaria software-development list with 4.9 stars and 15 verified reviews. That gives Accedia a second ranking signal beyond Clutch and The Manifest, while GoodFirms does not surface The B Team in the visible result text opened here (https://www.goodfirms.co/directory/country/top-software-development-companies/bulgaria).
Each peer's share of voice. Apify gives Lexis Solutions a separate marketplace voice with 25 reviews and a 5.0 rating. That makes Lexis visible to buyers looking for scraping, data, and AI-enabled data work, not only to buyers searching agency directories (https://apify.com/partners/find/lexis-solutions).
Each peer's share of voice. Clutch's Bulgaria AI-development page was updated on August 20, 2026 and does not contain The B Team in the visible page text searched here (https://clutch.co/bg/developers/artificial-intelligence). The same page lists Lexis Solutions with 32 reviews, Dreamix with 36 reviews, Scalefocus with 39 reviews, and Accedia with 40 reviews (https://clutch.co/bg/developers/artificial-intelligence).
Each peer's share of voice. Clutch adds recent-review momentum for selected peers on the AI-development page: Lexis Solutions had 2 reviews in the past six months, Dreamix had 2 reviews in the past six months, and Scalefocus had 3 reviews in the past six months (https://clutch.co/bg/developers/artificial-intelligence).
Each peer's share of voice. Clutch adds buyer-footprint signals for selected peers: Dreamix has completed reviewed projects in 11 countries, Accedia in 10 countries, and Scalefocus shows experience in 14 industries (https://clutch.co/bg/developers/artificial-intelligence).
Each peer's share of voice. DesignRush gives Lexis Solutions another public review and portfolio channel: it shows 3 DesignRush reviews, 17 Google reviews, and named portfolio entries for Onnoplus, Finansi.bg, StaffSquared, FranceVerif and Mindance (https://www.designrush.com/agency/profile/lexis-solutions).

verdicts.because: It directly uses the finding's core proof-volume comparison: selected peers have 32 to 40 Clutch reviews while The B Team has 8.

record.question: The buyer-review record is stronger than the employee-advocate record; which client advocates and which senior engineering voices can be safely brought into the proof system?
record.finding:
Advocates and critics. Clutch is the strongest advocate signal found: The B Team has an overall 5.0 rating from 8 reviews, with quality 5.0, schedule 4.9, cost 4.9 and willingness to refer 5.0 (https://clutch.co/profile/b-team).
Advocates and critics. Clutch says clients mention communication, high-quality work, unique expertise, exceeding expectations, honesty, transparency and flexibility (https://clutch.co/profile/b-team).
Advocates and critics. A verified Taggable review says The B Team built photo-sharing software with facial recognition, uploads, cloud storage and cross-platform support, and says the software processed over 1 million photos (https://clutch.co/profile/b-team).
Advocates and critics. A verified IT Broadcasting review says the client spent about $100,000, started around June 2022, and was still engaged when reviewed (https://clutch.co/profile/b-team).
Advocates and critics. A verified True Productions review says the client spent about $1 million, started in January 2016, and was still engaged when reviewed (https://clutch.co/profile/b-team).
Advocates and critics. The Manifest lists The B Team with 8 reviews, a 5.0 rating, 10-49 employees, Sofia location and services in web development, custom software development, web design and e-commerce (https://themanifest.com/bg/web-development/companies/sofia).
Advocates and critics. Clutch and The Manifest strengthen buyer trust, but they also show the market mostly hearing a software and web-development story, not a fully proven AI reputation story (https://clutch.co/profile/b-team; https://themanifest.com/bg/web-development/companies/sofia).
Advocates and critics. Clutch's current profile says project investments in reviews range from $68,000 to $1 million, and the most common project size is $50,000 to $199,999 based on seven reviews (https://clutch.co/profile/b-team). Clutch's current service split still starts with web development at 43%, then custom software development at 15%, then e-commerce, low/no-code and web design at 10% each (https://clutch.co/profile/b-team).
Advocates and critics. The IT Broadcasting Clutch review says The B Team helped build custom software for a patient-education product, using React Native, Gatsby, GraphQL, Azure Content Delivery Network and Azure Active Directory Single Sign-On (https://clutch.co/profile/b-team). That review says the work began around June 2022 and was ongoing at review time (https://clutch.co/profile/b-team).
Advocates and critics. The REAKT Agency Clutch review says The B Team was asked to audit a prior agency's site design before further development (https://clutch.co/profile/b-team). The review says the audit found problems from the original agency before those issues caused wider site failure (https://clutch.co/profile/b-team).
Advocates and critics. Agency Spotter lists The B Team with rating 0.0 and 0 client reviews, while also carrying a long promotional profile for the company (https://www.agencyspotter.com/the-b-team). C2CReview search results list The B Team with 0 reviews, 0 video reviews, 0 portfolios, 0 articles, and a trust score of 46 (https://c2creview.co/city/research/alcaniz).
Advocates and critics. Clutch ranks The B Team 17th on its Sofia web-development list, with an ability-to-deliver score of 31.6/40.0, reviews score of 16.2/20, clients-and-experience score of 10/10, and market-presence score of 5.4/10 (https://clutch.co/bg/web-developers/sofia).
Advocates and critics. Clutch ranks The B Team 3rd on its Bulgaria Drupal-developer list, with the same ability-to-deliver score of 31.6/40.0, reviews score of 16.2/20, clients-and-experience score of 10/10, and market-presence score of 5.4/10 (https://clutch.co/bg/developers/drupal).
Advocates and critics. Clutch's category pages strengthen the positive review record, but the low 5.4/10 market-presence score supports the brief's problem that the firm has limited public signal (https://clutch.co/bg/web-developers/sofia; https://clutch.co/bg/developers/drupal; bteam-blank-slate-brief.md).
Advocates and critics. YOX lists no opinions for Дъ Би Тийм OOD and invites anonymous employee opinion and salary submissions (https://yox.bg/%D0%B4%D1%8A-%D0%B1%D0%B8-%D1%82%D0%B8%D0%B9%D0%BC). This leaves the employee-advocate record thinner than the buyer-review record.
Advocates and critics. Third Party Pet is a partial external proof source, not an independent endorsement. The B Team names Third Party Pet in an owned case study (https://thebteam.com/case-studies/tpp-global). Third Party Pet's own site confirms the company and service category, but stays silent on The B Team's role in the fetched text (https://thirdpartypet.com/).
Advocates and critics. The public employee-advocate record remains thin. YOX lists Дъ Би Тийм with no opinions and invites anonymous employee opinions and salary information (https://yox.bg/%D0%B4%D1%8A-%D0%B1%D0%B8-%D1%82%D0%B8%D0%B9%D0%BC). DEV.BG says there are no current job ads from The B Team on its job board (https://dev.bg/company/the-b-team/).

verdicts.because: It directly uses the finding’s claim that Clutch/The Manifest buyer reviews are strong while the public employee-advocate record is thin, and asks which client advocates and engineering voices can support proof.

record.question: The EU AI Act, General Data Protection Regulation and buyer governance context make AI trust claims sensitive; what data-handling, model-use and human-review proof can The B Team show today?
record.finding:
Regulatory context. The B Team's own site claims Agentic AI Development, Workflow Automations and AI Company Upgrade services, so EU AI regulation is part of the operating context when work is placed on, used in, or affects people in the EU (https://thebteam.com/services; https://digital-strategy.ec.europa.eu/en/faqs/ai-literacy-questions-answers).
Regulatory context. The EU AI Act entered into force on 1 August 2024 and became generally applicable on 2 August 2026, while prohibited AI practices and AI literacy duties started on 2 February 2025 and general-purpose AI model obligations started on 2 August 2025 (https://digital-strategy.ec.europa.eu/en/policies/regulatory-framework-ai).
Regulatory context. The AI literacy duty applies to providers and deployers of AI systems, and Commission Q&A says Article 4 already applies from 2 February 2025 with supervision and enforcement rules applying from August 2026 (https://digital-strategy.ec.europa.eu/en/faqs/ai-literacy-questions-answers).
Regulatory context. AI Act Article 50 transparency duties apply from 2 August 2026 to certain generative and interactive AI systems and deepfakes, including duties to inform people when they interact directly with an AI system and to mark AI-generated or manipulated content (https://digital-strategy.ec.europa.eu/en/policies/guidelines-ai-transparency-obligations).
Regulatory context. High-risk AI classification is not established for The B Team, but the Commission says high-risk areas include biometrics, critical infrastructure, education, employment, migration, asylum and border control, with rules applying from 2 December 2027 for those areas and 2 August 2028 for regulated products (https://digital-strategy.ec.europa.eu/en/policies/guidelines-ai-high-risk-systems).
Regulatory context. Clutch reports a verified The B Team project involving facial-recognition photo features and Azure, so future public claims around biometric or image AI should be screened carefully instead of treated as ordinary web development proof (https://clutch.co/profile/b-team; https://digital-strategy.ec.europa.eu/en/policies/guidelines-ai-high-risk-systems).
Regulatory context. GDPR applies to small and medium-sized enterprises that process personal data, with some obligations depending on whether processing is core to the business or likely to create risk for individuals (https://commission.europa.eu/law/law-topic/data-protection/data-protection-explained_en).
Regulatory context. The European Commission says Standard Contractual Clauses can be used as a GDPR safeguard for transfers from the EU or EEA to third countries, which is material because The B Team serves both U.S. and European clients (https://commission.europa.eu/law/law-topic/data-protection/international-dimension-data-protection/standard-contractual-clauses-scc_en; https://thebteam.com/).
Regulatory context. The EU Data Act has applied since 12 September 2025, adding buyer context for data access, use and cloud contracts even where a small custom-development vendor is not the main regulated platform (https://digital-strategy.ec.europa.eu/en/policies/data-act).
Regulatory context. Bulgaria amended its Cybersecurity Act on 13 February 2026 to transpose NIS2, with expanded scope, cybersecurity risk measures, supply-chain security, training, and incident reporting at 24 hours, 72 hours and one month for covered entities (https://www.schoenherr.eu/content/bulgaria-implements-nis-2-directive-key-changes-to-the-cybersecurity-act).
Regulatory context. The EU Cyber Resilience Act entered into force on 10 December 2024; its main obligations apply from 11 December 2027 and reporting obligations apply from 11 September 2026 (https://digital-strategy.ec.europa.eu/en/policies/cyber-resilience-act).
Regulatory context. The Cyber Resilience Act applies to software or hardware products with digital elements made available on the EU market, so direct scope for The B Team depends on whether it markets software under its own name or trademark rather than only providing bespoke development services (https://digital-strategy.ec.europa.eu/en/policies/cra-summary).
Regulatory context. The Cyber Resilience Act requires manufacturers to perform a cybersecurity risk assessment, keep technical documentation, provide support-period information, handle vulnerabilities and run conformity assessment before placing covered products on the EU market (https://digital-strategy.ec.europa.eu/en/policies/cra-summary).
Regulatory context. The Cyber Resilience Act requires actively exploited vulnerability and severe-incident notices through the CRA reporting route, with 24-hour early warning, 72-hour main notice, and later final reports depending on the event (https://digital-strategy.ec.europa.eu/en/policies/cra-summary).
Regulatory context. The Commission's 2026 guidance for general-purpose AI model providers says only significant modifications to AI models trigger provider obligations, while minor modifications do not, so The B Team should distinguish model integration from model-provider activity in any public AI claim (https://digital-strategy.ec.europa.eu/en/policies/guidelines-gpai-providers).
Regulatory context. The same guidance says Commission enforcement powers for general-purpose AI provider obligations start on 2 August 2026, and providers of models placed on the market before 2 August 2025 must comply by 2 August 2027 (https://digital-strategy.ec.europa.eu/en/policies/guidelines-gpai-providers).
Regulatory context. The European Data Protection Board's AI-model opinion says anonymity must be assessed case by case, and an AI model is anonymous only where identification or extraction of personal data is very unlikely, which matters for AI projects using client, user or scraped data (https://www.edpb.europa.eu/news/edpb-opinion-on-ai-models-gdpr-principles-support-responsible-ai_en).
Regulatory context. The same EDPB opinion says legitimate interest can support some AI development or deployment only if processing is strictly necessary and the rights-balancing test is met, and unlawfully processed development data can affect later use unless the model has been properly anonymized (https://www.edpb.europa.eu/news/edpb-opinion-on-ai-models-gdpr-principles-support-responsible-ai_en).
Regulatory context. DORA has applied from 17 January 2025 and requires financial entities to manage ICT risk, report incidents, test resilience and govern ICT third-party providers, so The B Team's finance-sector work may face buyer due-diligence demands even if direct DORA designation is not established (https://finance.ec.europa.eu/news/digital-finance-2024-12-19_en).
Regulatory context. The new EU Product Liability Directive entered into force on 8 December 2024, must be transposed by EU countries by 9 December 2026, and applies to products placed on the EU market from 9 December 2026. It is built for new technologies including artificial intelligence and covers damage including destruction or corruption of data, so The B Team should separate bespoke services from any software or AI product it places on the EU market (https://single-market-economy.ec.europa.eu/single-market/goods/free-movement-sectors/liability-defective-products_en).
Regulatory context. The same EU Product Liability Directive seeks to ensure there is an EU-based liable party even where the manufacturer is outside the EU. This matters for The B Team's U.S.-Europe work because any claim about ownership, deployment, resale or support of AI software may affect who is treated as the liable economic operator (https://single-market-economy.ec.europa.eu/single-market/goods/free-movement-sectors/liability-defective-products_en).
Regulatory context. The European Commission says a company using a third-party contact list for direct marketing must be able to show GDPR-compliant collection, respect objections, inform people at first contact, and comply with ePrivacy rules for email marketing. This is material to a proof-building plan that may use founder outreach, referral lists, events or CRM exports (https://commission.europa.eu/law/law-topic/data-protection/information-business-and-organisations/legal-grounds-processing-data/can-data-received-third-party-be-used-marketing_en).
Regulatory context. The FTC says advertising claims must be truthful, not deceptive or unfair, and evidence-based, including for online advertising that sells software, apps or other services. This adds U.S. claim-risk context to The B Team's AI-forward message for U.S. buyers (https://www.ftc.gov/business-guidance/advertising-marketing).
Regulatory context. The FTC says model-as-a-service companies may be liable if they break privacy commitments, including promises not to use customer data to train or update models through direct or indirect methods. This is relevant even if The B Team integrates third-party models, because U.S. buyers may ask how client data, prompts and outputs are handled across providers (https://www.ftc.gov/policy/advocacy-research/tech-at-ftc/2024/01/ai-companies-uphold-your-privacy-confidentiality-commitments).
Regulatory context. The B Team privacy-policy search result says, "We do not use your personal data for automated decision-making or profiling" with legal or similar significant effects. Independent public sources opened in this pass stayed silent on that claim, and the opened page did not expose a detailed data-processing agreement, subprocessor list or AI-data-use terms (https://thebteam.com/privacy-policy).
Regulatory context. NIST's AI Risk Management Framework is voluntary and is meant to help organizations build trustworthiness into the design, development, use and evaluation of AI products, services and systems. NIST released a Generative AI profile on 26 July 2024 and updated that profile page on 8 April 2026, making NIST a likely buyer reference point for U.S.-facing AI governance proof (https://www.nist.gov/itl/ai-risk-management-framework; https://www.nist.gov/publications/artificial-intelligence-risk-management-framework-generative-artificial-intelligence).
Regulatory context. The B Team privacy-policy search result says the policy was dated 15 March 2026 and says the company is committed to protecting privacy under GDPR (https://thebteam.com/privacy-policy).
Regulatory context. The B Team privacy-policy search result says, “All third-party service providers are contractually bound to process your data only on our instructions and in compliance with the GDPR”; no independent public source opened in this pass corroborated those contracts (https://thebteam.com/privacy-policy).
Regulatory context. The European Accessibility Act covers products and services including computers and operating systems, banking services, e-books, and e-commerce, which matters when The B Team builds consumer-facing EU digital services for clients (https://commission.europa.eu/strategy-and-policy/policies/justice-and-fundamental-rights/disability/european-accessibility-act-eaa_en).
Regulatory context. The European Accessibility Act summary says the rules apply from 28 June 2025 to covered products and services (https://eur-lex.europa.eu/EN/legal-content/summary/accessibility-of-products-and-services.html).
Regulatory context. The EU Cyber Solidarity Act entered into force on 4 February 2025 and aims to improve EU detection, preparation, and response to major cybersecurity threats and attacks (https://digital-strategy.ec.europa.eu/en/policies/cyber-solidarity).
Regulatory context. The EU Cyber Solidarity Act includes a European Cybersecurity Alert System made of national and cross-border cyber hubs, which use AI and data analytics to detect threats and share warnings across borders (https://digital-strategy.ec.europa.eu/en/policies/cyber-solidarity).

verdicts.because: It engages the finding by naming the EU AI Act and GDPR regulatory context and asking for The B Team-specific proof on data handling, model use, human review, and buyer governance tied to its AI services.

It directly uses the finding’s EU AI Act and GDPR regulatory context and asks for The B Team-specific proof on data handling, model use, and human review, which matches the finding’s claims about AI services, AI-data-use terms, model-provider distinctions, and buyer governance expectations.

record.question: Gartner and other market sources show agentic AI demand and skepticism rising together; where should The B Team draw the line between AI ambition and proven delivery?
record.finding:
Category context. The B Team sits in a crowded Bulgarian software category: the U.S. Country Commercial Guide says Bulgaria has about 10,000 ICT companies, 70 percent of which export, and calls Bulgaria a top ICT outsourcing destination (https://www.trade.gov/country-commercial-guides/bulgaria-information-and-communications-technologies).
Category context. The same U.S. guide says Bulgaria's ICT revenue rose 300 percent over seven years to EUR 2.5 billion and that software is the best-performing ICT segment after 16 years of EU membership (https://www.trade.gov/country-commercial-guides/bulgaria-information-and-communications-technologies).
Category context. The Manifest lists The B Team among Bulgarian software developers with 8 reviews, a 5.0 rating, 10-49 employees, Sofia location and 2017 establishment, while nearby listings include AI Agents and larger Sofia competitors such as Accedia and Scalefocus (https://themanifest.com/bg/software-development/companies).
Category context. Clutch lists The B Team at $50-$99 per hour, 10-49 employees, Sofia, founded 2017, and service mix led by 43 percent web development and 15 percent custom software development, which supports the brief's warning that the public profile still reads more like software services than AI specialist (https://clutch.co/profile/b-team).
Category context. Clutch independently corroborates delivery proof through a verified Taggable review: a March 2019 ongoing custom software engagement, $50,000 to $199,999 range, about $140,000 spent, Azure and APIs, facial-recognition photo features, and over 1 million photos processed (https://clutch.co/profile/b-team).
Category context. H512 describes The B Team Ltd. as a software company serving U.S. clients in finance, retail, healthcare, entertainment and digital communications, with 30 employees worldwide and 20 in Bulgaria, which corroborates the supplied brief's sector range and headcount range (https://h512.com/company/the-b-team/).
Category context. Gartner's 2026 agentic-AI cycle says only 17 percent of organizations have deployed AI agents, while more than 60 percent expect to do so within two years, so demand is high but proof of real delivery is still scarce (https://www.gartner.com/en/articles/hype-cycle-for-agentic-ai).
Category context. Gartner says agentic AI is at the "Peak of Inflated Expectations" and that fully autonomous agents are not ready for most enterprise uses, which makes an unqualified AI-agent claim risky for a small vendor with thin public proof (https://www.gartner.com/en/articles/hype-cycle-for-agentic-ai).
Category context. Gartner predicted in August 2025 that 40 percent of enterprise applications would include task-specific AI agents by the end of 2026, up from less than 5 percent at the time, which supports The B Team's AI-market opportunity (https://www.gartner.com/en/newsroom/press-releases/2025-08-26-gartner-predicts-40-percent-of-enterprise-apps-will-feature-task-specific-ai-agents-by-2026-up-from-less-than-5-percent-in-2025).
Category context. Gartner also predicts that by 2027, 40 percent of enterprises will demote or shut down autonomous AI agents because governance gaps are found only after production incidents, so The B Team's category proof should cover autonomy level, access limits, approvals, logs, rollback and ownership (https://www.gartner.com/en/newsroom/press-releases/2026-05-26-gartner-says-applying-uniform-governance-across-ai-agents-will-lead-to-enterprise-ai-agent-failure).
Category context. McKinsey's 2026 AI Trust Maturity Survey says only about 30 percent of organizations reach maturity level three or higher in strategy, governance and agentic-AI controls, which makes trust architecture a buyer concern rather than a legal footnote (https://www.mckinsey.com/capabilities/tech-and-ai/our-insights/tech-forward/state-of-ai-trust-in-2026-shifting-to-the-agentic-era).
Category context. Stanford's 2026 AI Index says organizational AI adoption reached 88 percent, SWE-bench Verified coding performance rose from 60 percent to near 100 percent in one year, and AI agents improved from 12 percent to about 66 percent task success on OSWorld while still failing about one in three attempts, which frames both the opportunity and the reliability gap in The B Team's market (https://hai.stanford.edu/ai-index/2026-ai-index-report).
Category context. Agency Spotter lists The B Team under Custom Software Developers, not AI development. It lists automotive industry experience, agency size 50-100, B2B and B2C audience scope, and 0.0 rating with 0 client reviews. This directory profile adds no independent AI proof and keeps the public category signal closer to software services than AI specialist (https://www.agencyspotter.com/the-b-team).
Category context. Agency Spotter says The B Team is a "leading website and mobile app development company" with over 40 developers working U.S. hours and offering work at "a fraction of the cost in the United States." That profile reinforces the generic nearshore-cost message the supplied brief says should not be the central idea (https://www.agencyspotter.com/the-b-team; bteam-blank-slate-brief.md).
Category context. H512 lists a conventional engineering stack: C#, PHP, MSSQL Server, MS T-SQL, MySQL/PostgreSQL, JavaScript, HTML and CSS, Python, Laravel, Angular, React, Spring, Django, Rails, Node.js, Bootstrap, jQuery, CodeIgniter and ASP.net. That supports the banked finding that public proof is strongest for software delivery, not current agentic-AI work (https://h512.com/company/the-b-team/).
Category context. BASSCOM's homepage presents Bulgaria's software sector as export-led, with 87 percent export revenue and 11.5 percent growth shown on the page. This strengthens the category context that The B Team competes in a mature export-software market rather than an empty AI niche (https://basscom.org/en).
Category context. GoodFirms says it reviewed 121 verified software development companies in Bulgaria as of August 2026, with a median hourly rate of USD 37, a median rating of 4.9, and 21 percent employing 50 or more people (https://www.goodfirms.co/directory/country/top-software-development-companies/bulgaria).
Category context. GoodFirms says the top-ranked Bulgarian software firm on its August 2026 page is Accedia, with a 4.9 rating, 15 verified reviews, Sofia headquarters, and 2012 founding (https://www.goodfirms.co/directory/country/top-software-development-companies/bulgaria).
Category context. Clutch’s August 20, 2026 Bulgaria AI page did not contain the text “The B Team,” while it did show AI-category peers with agent, AI development, AI consulting, and generative AI service mixes (https://clutch.co/bg/developers/artificial-intelligence).
Category context. Clutch’s Bulgaria AI page lists VECTOR Labs in Sofia with 55 percent AI Agents, 20 percent AI Consulting, 20 percent AI Development, 14 reviews, and a 5.0 rating (https://clutch.co/bg/developers/artificial-intelligence).
Category context. Clutch’s Bulgaria AI page lists Exelor in Plovdiv with 35 percent AI Agents, 25 percent AI Consulting, 10 percent Custom Software Development, 10 percent Generative AI, seven reviews, and a 5.0 rating (https://clutch.co/bg/developers/artificial-intelligence).

verdicts.because: It engages the finding by using its Gartner agentic-AI demand/skepticism facts and its claim that The B Team has thin public AI proof versus stronger software-delivery evidence.
It engages the finding by using its specific Gartner agentic-AI demand/skepticism tension and The B Team’s gap between AI ambition and publicly proven delivery.

record.question: Bulgaria's software market is mature and export-led; what Bulgarian, European or founder-led proof should The B Team use so it is not heard as another nearshore supplier?
record.finding:
Geopolitical context. The B Team's cross-border market is explicit because its site says it is headquartered in Sofia and serves clients across the United States and Europe, and its public contact footprint includes Sofia and Spain (https://thebteam.com/).
Geopolitical context. Bulgaria's position as an EU-based export ICT hub supports The B Team's nearshore story because the U.S. Country Commercial Guide says 70 percent of about 10,000 Bulgarian ICT companies are export-only (https://www.trade.gov/country-commercial-guides/bulgaria-information-and-communications-technologies).
Geopolitical context. The World Economic Forum's 2026 Global Risks Report says geoeconomic confrontation was selected as the top risk most likely to trigger a material global crisis in 2026, with state-based armed conflict next, making cross-border buyer trust and continuity proof material for a Bulgaria-based firm serving U.S. and EU clients (https://www.weforum.org/publications/global-risks-report-2026/digest/).
Geopolitical context. The same World Economic Forum report ranks misinformation and disinformation second and cyber insecurity sixth in the two-year outlook, and says adverse outcomes of AI rises from 30th in the two-year outlook to fifth in the 10-year outlook, which makes AI trust claims a live context risk (https://www.weforum.org/publications/global-risks-report-2026/digest/).
Geopolitical context. The European Commission's 2026 Digital Decade country report says Bulgaria has a dynamic ICT sector but that SME uptake of AI, cloud and data analytics remains limited, which gives The B Team an opportunity to stand out but also raises buyer proof expectations (https://digital-strategy.ec.europa.eu/en/factpages/bulgarias-2026-digital-decade-country-report).
Geopolitical context. The OECD says Bulgaria's AI policy is guided by a 2020 national strategy with pillars including infrastructure, education, research, data, sector innovation and ethical AI, but that the strategy lacks a clear action plan with implementation activities and timelines (https://www.oecd.org/en/publications/progress-in-implementing-the-european-union-coordinated-plan-on-artificial-intelligence-volume-1_6d530a88-en/bulgaria_26e81b51-en.html).
Geopolitical context. The OECD also says Bulgaria has Discoverer and HEMUS supercomputing facilities running, Avitohol under development, INSAIT established in 2023, and BgGPT as the country's first open-source Bulgarian-language model, which supports a national AI ecosystem story around Sofia and Bulgaria (https://www.oecd.org/en/publications/progress-in-implementing-the-european-union-coordinated-plan-on-artificial-intelligence-volume-1_6d530a88-en/bulgaria_26e81b51-en.html).
Geopolitical context. The European Commission adopted the EU-U.S. Data Privacy Framework adequacy decision on 10 July 2023, allowing personal data to flow freely from the EU to participating U.S. companies, which is material to The B Team's U.S. and Europe client base (https://commission.europa.eu/law/law-topic/data-protection/international-dimension-data-protection/eu-us-data-transfers_en).
Geopolitical context. The Commission published the first review of that adequacy decision on 9 October 2024, so transatlantic data-transfer assurance has an active review history rather than being a settled background assumption (https://commission.europa.eu/law/law-topic/data-protection/international-dimension-data-protection/adequacy-decisions_en).
Geopolitical context. Stanford's 2026 AI Index says the United States had 5,427 AI data centers and that nearly all leading AI chips depend on one Taiwanese foundry, while U.S. AI talent inflow has dropped 89 percent since 2017, making AI supply-chain and talent geography part of the context for an EU-based AI services partner (https://hai.stanford.edu/ai-index/2026-ai-index-report).
Geopolitical context. Stanford's 2026 AI Index says national AI strategies and state-backed AI supercomputing are rising, but model production remains concentrated in the United States and China, which reinforces the need for a Sofia-based firm to state clearly whether it builds, adapts, integrates or governs third-party models (https://hai.stanford.edu/ai-index/2026-ai-index-report).
Geopolitical context. The European Commission's Apply AI Strategy is designed to strengthen EU technological sovereignty and boost AI adoption across Europe, especially among small and medium-sized enterprises. It also promotes a buy-European approach for the public sector and focuses on open-source AI solutions, which can support an EU-based vendor story but also raises questions about dependence on non-European models and cloud providers (https://digital-strategy.ec.europa.eu/en/policies/apply-ai).
Geopolitical context. The Commission says 19 AI Factories and 13 antennas are being set up, with at least 9 new AI-optimised supercomputers planned to more than triple EuroHPC AI computing capacity. These facilities are open to European users across industry, research, academia and public authorities (https://digital-strategy.ec.europa.eu/en/policies/ai-factories).
Geopolitical context. CORDIS says the EU-funded BRAIN++ project will establish Bulgaria's first AI Factory and create a national hub for foundation-model development, adaptation and deployment. It says the project addresses gaps in computing infrastructure, specialised models, governance frameworks, talent development and cross-sector support (https://cordis.europa.eu/project/id/101250707).
Geopolitical context. CORDIS says BRAIN++ plans four specialised models: a 175-billion-parameter Bulgarian-language BgGPT, RoboticsBG for manufacturing and logistics, FORSE for earth-observation use cases, and MEDBG for healthcare. It also plans COMPL-AI, a compliance framework aligned with the EU AI Act (https://cordis.europa.eu/project/id/101250707).
Geopolitical context. The 2026 Digital Decade Eurobarometer says 74 percent of Bulgarians consider digital policy a high EU priority (https://digital-strategy.ec.europa.eu/en/factpages/bulgarias-2026-digital-decade-country-report).
Geopolitical context. The same Eurobarometer says 91 percent of Bulgarian respondents rank protecting online privacy and security as the top priority for the next decade (https://digital-strategy.ec.europa.eu/en/factpages/bulgarias-2026-digital-decade-country-report).
Geopolitical context. The same Eurobarometer says 76 percent of Bulgarian respondents agree AI development should be carefully regulated to ensure safety, even if that may constrain developers (https://digital-strategy.ec.europa.eu/en/factpages/bulgarias-2026-digital-decade-country-report).
Geopolitical context. The same Eurobarometer says Bulgarian concerns about generative AI are privacy and data protection at 34 percent, ethical issues or potential misuse at 32 percent, and accuracy or incorrect information at 31 percent (https://digital-strategy.ec.europa.eu/en/factpages/bulgarias-2026-digital-decade-country-report).
Geopolitical context. Bulgaria’s national Digital Decade roadmap has 60 measures with a total budget of EUR 2.19 billion, and 48 percent of those measures are set to expire by the end of 2026 (https://digital-strategy.ec.europa.eu/en/factpages/bulgarias-2026-digital-decade-country-report).
Geopolitical context. The same report says Bulgaria has an estimated 112 edge nodes and one unicorn in 2025 (https://digital-strategy.ec.europa.eu/en/factpages/bulgarias-2026-digital-decade-country-report).

verdicts.because: It directly uses the finding's Bulgaria export-led ICT hub/nearshore story and The B Team proof-expectation claim by asking what Bulgarian, European or founder-led proof can distinguish it from another nearshore supplier.
It engages the finding through Bulgaria being an export-led ICT hub, The B Team's Sofia/EU-to-U.S. nearshore positioning, and the need for proof to distinguish it from generic nearshore suppliers.

record.question: The B Team's reputation problem is not weak capability; it is that the public proof system has not caught up with the AI-era story the company now wants buyers to believe. The white space is a proof-first AI software partner that shows exactly where its AI claim is true, where its public record still proves enterprise software craft better than AI depth, and where larger peers compete through scale and broader proof libraries. The strategy should first make the company easier to trust, then make it more visible.
record.finding:
AI proof gap. The company's newer AI positioning is not matched by AI-specific Clutch service lines; Clutch lists web development at 43%, custom software development at 15%, e-commerce at 10%, low/no-code at 10%, web design at 10%, ERP consulting and system integration at 5%, IT staff augmentation at 5%, and IoT at 2% (https://clutch.co/profile/b-team). (bears on: Constraints, guardrails & AI permissions)
Positioning-history pattern. The public-positioning trail now shows at least three eras: the older 'Offshore Like Next Door' platform, the 14 October 2022 website relaunch around that idea, and the 2026 AI-first site language (banked findings; https://thebteam.com/news; https://bg.linkedin.com/company/the-b-team-real; https://thebteam.com/). (bears on: Reputation problem / desired perception)
Each peer's share of voice. The B Team has 8 Clutch reviews, 10-49 employees, and a $50-$99 hourly rate. Clutch lists its common project size as $50,000-$199,999 based on 7 reviews (https://clutch.co/profile/b-team).
Each peer's share of voice. Lexis Solutions has 32 Clutch reviews, 10-49 employees, and appears on Clutch's Top Artificial Intelligence Companies in Sofia page with 25% AI consulting and 10% AI development. Its visible review count is four times The B Team's count (https://clutch.co/bg/developers/artificial-intelligence/sofia; https://clutch.co/profile/lexis-solutions).
Each peer's share of voice. Dreamix has 36 Clutch reviews, 250-999 employees, and a most common Clutch project size of $200,000-$999,999. Its visible proof volume is much larger than The B Team's 8-review record (https://clutch.co/profile/dreamix).
Each peer's share of voice. Accedia has 40 Clutch reviews, 250-999 employees, and service lines including 20% custom software development, 20% web development, and 15% AI development. Its visible review count is five times The B Team's count (https://clutch.co/profile/accedia).
Each peer's share of voice. Scalefocus has 39 Clutch reviews, 250-999 employees, and reports 1000+ projects across 26 countries for more than 300 clients. Its public proof base is far larger than The B Team's visible proof base (https://clutch.co/profile/scalefocus).
Each peer's share of voice. The Manifest's Bulgaria software-development list gives Dreamix 36 reviews and places it above Accedia, Scalefocus and Lexis Solutions in the visible ranking. It also lists VistaJet as a Dreamix client, adding a named proof signal not in the banked record (https://themanifest.com/bg/software-development/companies).
Each peer's share of voice. The Manifest's same list gives Accedia 40 reviews, Scalefocus 39 reviews and Lexis Solutions 32 reviews, while The B Team appears much later with 8 reviews. That repeats the banked pattern on a second directory: The B Team's visible proof base is smaller than each selected peer's (https://themanifest.com/bg/software-development/companies).
Each peer's share of voice. The Manifest's “most new reviews in the past 12 months” table names Dreamix with 7 new reviews, Lexis Solutions with 5 new reviews and Scalefocus with 3 new reviews. The B Team does not appear in the visible top 13 for new reviews, so its review momentum also trails selected peers on that source (https://themanifest.com/bg/software-development/companies).
Each peer's share of voice. Clutch's Top 13 Sofia AI Consulting Firms page lists Lexis Solutions at number 2 with a 37.3/40 ability-to-deliver score, 19/20 reviews score, 10/10 clients-and-experience score and 8.3/10 market-presence score. The B Team, Dreamix, Accedia and Scalefocus did not appear in the page text searched in this pass, so Lexis has a clearer AI-consulting directory signal than the selected peer set there (https://clutch.co/bg/consulting/ai/sofia).
Each peer's share of voice. LinkedIn adds a clear visibility ladder among the selected peers: Scalefocus shows 46,212 followers, Dreamix 20,339, Accedia 9,226, and Lexis Solutions 1,611. The B Team shows 136 followers, so its company-channel reach trails all four selected peers by a wide margin (https://bg.linkedin.com/company/scalefocus; https://bg.linkedin.com/company/dreamix-ltd; https://www.linkedin.com/company/accedia; https://bg.linkedin.com/company/lexis-solutions; https://bg.linkedin.com/company/the-b-team-real).
Each peer's share of voice. GoodFirms ranks Accedia first on its Bulgaria software-development list with 4.9 stars and 15 verified reviews. That gives Accedia a second ranking signal beyond Clutch and The Manifest, while GoodFirms does not surface The B Team in the visible result text opened here (https://www.goodfirms.co/directory/country/top-software-development-companies/bulgaria).
Each peer's share of voice. Apify gives Lexis Solutions a separate marketplace voice with 25 reviews and a 5.0 rating. That makes Lexis visible to buyers looking for scraping, data, and AI-enabled data work, not only to buyers searching agency directories (https://apify.com/partners/find/lexis-solutions).

# Pre-Engagement Briefing Pack

Six AI (artificial intelligence) desk audits, a provisional hypothesis and a working style calibration before the client conversation. Anything unconfirmed is a gap, not a finding.

## How to use this pack

Terms, context and next steps orient the reader.

### Terms

- desk audit — the pre-conversation read of what public sources say about the client; six named passes over the material the workflow already has
- finding — something one of the audits established from those public sources
- gap — something one of the audits could not establish; it is listed as still to check rather than stated as a finding
- provisional hypothesis — a one-paragraph point of view written to be tested by the research that follows, not defended
- Client Style Note — the read of how the client writes about itself in its own published communications; the tone and vocabulary a document written for this client should mirror
- question bank — the starter set of interview questions the operator sharpens for the client conversation, each one built on a specific desk-audit finding
- independent assessment — the challenge to the client's own words, checked against independent public sources and paired with one of three verdicts (corroborated, challenged, unverified)
- high-trust input — a claim independently corroborated by a public source, so downstream work can build on it without re-verifying

### Context

This is the pre-engagement briefing pack -- what the engine knows about the client before anyone speaks to them. It sits between the ingestion of the supplied material and the operator's review, and no downstream phase acts on it until that review has been completed.

### Next steps

Read each audit section, judge whether it carries you into a client conversation, and answer the "Open -- waiting on a person" section at the end. Nothing after Phase 2 runs until the point of view and the style calibration each carry an approved decision with a name against it; the question bank travels on as a draft.

## Engagement frame

## Outputs and success

| Evidence base and readiness check; Positioning options; Corporate reputation platform and message architecture; Pillar architecture; Stakeholder and founder-visibility map; Twelve-month reputation roadmap; Measurement framework aligned to AMEC Barcelona Principles 4.0 and the AMEC Integrated Evaluation Framework | Checks readiness and identifies gaps before strategy writing starts.; Resists inventing proof where evidence is thin.; Shows positioning options before recommendation.; Separates facts, missing inputs, conflicting signals and strategic judgment.; Produces a lean strategy a founder-led small team can run.; Makes the message architecture and proof model the first client-facing decision artifact. |

## Communication guardrails and proof

| Control | This engagement |
| --- | --- |
| Must say | The firm has real enterprise software delivery substance.; The AI repositioning must be connected to verifiable capability and delivery evidence.; Trust must be built through proof, consistency, founder credibility and client or reference validation. |
| Must avoid | Do not overstate AI capability, certifications, client wins or metrics.; Do not invent client names, case studies, project specifics or proof points.; Do not rely on generic nearshore claims as the central idea.; Do not ignore public-source inconsistencies. |
| Proof ladder | named reference > anonymous but verifiable reference > artifact > demo |
| Do not say | Do not say The B Team is a proven agentic AI leader unless named or verifiable proof supports it.; Do not claim AI certifications unless the client provides evidence.; Do not invent client names, project specifics, metrics or case studies.; Do not use founding-year or headcount claims until the client reconciles the public record.; Do not make generic nearshore-cost claims the central idea. |
| Claim rules | Separate public fact, client-supplied claim, conflicting signal, gap and strategic judgment.; Use AI claims only inside the proof boundary the evidence supports.; Mark client-owned claims as owner-published unless an independent source corroborates them.; Use public client names only where they are already public and relevant.; Treat hypotheses as provisional until client evidence confirms or overturns them. |

The B Team's reputation problem is not weak capability; it is that the public proof system has not caught up with the AI-era story the company now wants buyers to believe. sections.text:
The B Team presents itself as “an AI development company headquartered in Sofia, Bulgaria,” delivering enterprise software, AI-powered automation and architect-led delivery since 2009; its current menu is Hand-Crafted Development, Agentic AI Development, Workflow Automations and AI Company Upgrade, under the line “The speed of AI. The soul of craftsmanship.” [The B Team site]

The independent proof base is older and software-led: H512 says software and hardware product development for US clients, Clutch shows web, custom software, ERP, medical technology, mobile, Azure, Salesforce Lightning, WooCommerce, WordPress, Drupal and Umbraco work, DEV.BG lists a broad stack from C#/.NET, PHP and SQL to Python, Laravel, React, Django and Node.js, and Bulgarian records classify the entity as computer programming. [H512; Clutch; DEV.BG; Company Guru]

The firm sells senior engineering capability to companies, not consumers, with a US/EU buyer focus; Clutch lists $50-$99 hourly rates, 10-49 employees, 60% enterprise clients, 20% midmarket, 20% small business, reviewed investments from $68,000 to $1 million, and a common project size of $50,000-$199,999. [Brief; The B Team site; Clutch]

Public scale is inconsistent: Papagal reports 2021 turnover of BGN 1,062,000, down 2% from BGN 1,085,000 in 2020, seven employees in 2021, 2020 assets of BGN 703,000 and equity of BGN 132,000; H512 says 30 worldwide and 20 in Bulgaria, Clutch’s location block says 31-40, LinkedIn says 51-200, and Agency Spotter says 50-100. [Papagal; H512; Clutch; LinkedIn; Agency Spotter]

The legal entity is Дъ Би Тийм OOD / The B Team, UIC 203913310, registered on 9 February 2016, VAT-registered on 27 January 2017, with capital converted from BGN 100 to EUR 51 on 26 January 2026; current ownership appears 50% Kamen Borislavov Kamenov directly and 50% Matthew Maday indirectly through Main Assembly EOOD. [Papagal; CompanyBook]

Still to check: completed agentic-AI delivery, AI outcomes, 2022-2025 financials, revenue split, margin, retention, client concentration, current office model, cap table rights, full leadership bench, investor materials and usable annual-report figures. [Banked gaps]

The reputation record is high-sentiment but low-footprint: visibility sits in directories, review platforms, employer listings, LinkedIn and owned channels rather than mainstream media or analyst coverage. [Clutch; The Manifest; H512; LinkedIn]

Clutch is the strongest advocacy surface, with 8 reviews, 5.0 overall, 5.0 quality, 4.9 schedule, 4.9 cost and 5.0 willingness to refer; review themes include communication, high-quality work, expertise, transparency, project management, client-team fit and straightforward pricing. [Clutch]

The Manifest repeats 8 reviews and 5.0 overall, but it is a Clutch sister site and should be treated as distribution of the same proof ecosystem rather than a wholly independent proof base. [The Manifest; Clutch Help]

The strongest public outcomes are software outcomes: Taggable’s Azure and API photo platform with facial recognition processed more than 1 million photos, IT Broadcasting spent about $100,000 on React Native, Gatsby, GraphQL, Azure CDN and Azure SSO work from June 2022, and a digital rewards platform supported 1,000 global rewards in 23 currencies. [Clutch]

The central reputation risk is inconsistency: the site says since 2009, H512 says 2015, Bulgarian records show 2016, and LinkedIn, Clutch and The Manifest say 2017; the site leads with AI, while Clutch still shows 43% web development, 15% custom software, 10% e-commerce, 10% low/no-code, 10% web design, 5% ERP, 5% staff augmentation and 2% IoT. [The B Team site; H512; Papagal; LinkedIn; Clutch; The Manifest]

Search is weak on name alone because unrelated entities include bteam.org’s US nonprofit, thebteam.in’s event-marketing business, B-Team Consulting at b-team.co, B-Team Jiu Jitsu, B Team Ottawa and The B Team Podcast. [B Team nonprofit; The B Team India; B-Team Consulting; search results]

Still to check: earned-media volume, social sentiment, analyst narrative, AI-specific rankings, litigation, regulator action, Redmine exposure and share of search against duplicate-name entities. [Banked gaps]

The owned web system is live at thebteam.com with Home, About Us, Services, Our Process, Case Studies, Lab, News and Privacy Policy, and the site publishes Sofia and Spain contact locations, a US phone number, info@yourbteam.com and sales@yourbteam.com. [The B Team site]

The channel system is split: thebteam.com carries the current brand, while yourbteam.com remains in email and Redmine paths, H512 still links yourbteam.com, and BigDomainData dates yourbteam.com to 17 September 2015 with expiry on 17 September 2026. [The B Team site; H512; Redmine; BigDomainData]

LinkedIn is live as The B Team - Real with 136 followers, 9 discoverable employees, Sofia headquarters, 51-200 employees, “Outsourcing and Offshoring Consulting,” and the older “Offshore Like Next Door™” promise. [LinkedIn]

The public voice is not yet unified: the homepage says “The speed of AI. The soul of craftsmanship,” the About result says global engineering should feel like a local partnership and “We rescue brittle, high-risk software that your team is afraid to touch,” Facebook uses “Choose Offshore like Next Door,” and a News snippet calls the 2022 Christmas party a “debaucherous spectacle.” [The B Team site; Facebook]

Community proof is buyer-led rather than social-led: Clutch names REAKT Agency, IT Broadcasting, True Productions, Taggable, Any All Every and BigScore Engagement Solutions, with working rhythms across Redmine, Zoom, Dropbox, email, weekly calls and daily calls in busy periods. [Clutch]

Matthew Maday is the visible founder voice across Clutch, LinkedIn, Substack and Main Assembly; his Substack shows May 2026 posts on AI-era work, memory and founder purpose, while Kamen Kamenov is mainly visible in official, employer and registry-style records. [Clutch; LinkedIn; Substack; Main Assembly; H512; registry sources]

Still to check: official X, Instagram, YouTube, GitHub, current posting cadence, owned community, Facebook engagement, Substack subscriber count, Kamen Kamenov’s public channel and approved voice hierarchy. [Banked gaps]

The relevant peer set is four Bulgarian software-services competitors: Lexis Solutions as the small AI-native specialist, Dreamix as the acquired enterprise unit, Accedia as the premium independent firm, and Scalefocus as the acquisition-built scale player. [Clutch; LinkedIn; Dreamix; Accedia; Scalefocus]

Lexis is Sofia-based, 10-49 employees, founded in 2017, with Los Angeles and Berlin locations, 32 Clutch reviews, 25% AI consulting, 10% AI development, a “Ship one AI workflow in 14 days” offer, Apify marketplace proof with 25 reviews and 5.0, and case claims around Onno Plus, Finansi.bg and governed enterprise AI assistants. [Clutch; Lexis Solutions; Apify; The Manifest]

Dreamix has 36 Clutch reviews, 250-999 employees, enterprise AI and bespoke software positioning, 20+ years’ experience, 300+ AI-enabled engineers, 95% employee retention, Coca-Cola HBC and CERN proof, and became part of Synechron in a deal that closed on 26 March 2024 with undisclosed terms. [Clutch; Dreamix; Synechron; SeeNews; CEE Legal Matters]

Accedia has 40 Clutch reviews, 250-999 employees, 250+ engineers, 549+ projects, 150+ clients, 20+ countries, 91% client retention, ISO proof, a 2020 AI Capability Center, self-published 50+ AI projects, and 2026 AI award claims partly corroborated by award bodies. [Clutch; Accedia; Business Intelligence Group; Brilliance Awards]

Scalefocus has 39 Clutch reviews, 250-999 employees, 1000+ projects in 26 countries for 300+ clients, Upnetix and Centroida acquisitions, and a sovereign-AI product story through AION, with Globee wins and a PRNewswire release saying it was validated across more than 30 production use cases. [Clutch; Scalefocus; Novinite; Globee; PRNewswire]

The B Team trails all four on visible proof volume and LinkedIn reach: 8 Clutch reviews and 136 LinkedIn followers versus Lexis 1,611, Accedia 9,226, Dreamix 20,339 and Scalefocus 46,212. [Clutch; LinkedIn]

Still to check: deal values, paid media, conference visibility, independent peer narrative, measured share of voice, buyer win-loss data and any AI-ranking position for The B Team. [Banked gaps]

Approval power is concentrated: owners and managers matter first because public records list Kamen Borislavov Kamenov with 50%, Main Assembly EOOD with 50%, and Kamen Kamenov plus Matthew G. Maday as managers. [Papagal; CompanyBook]

Main Assembly is both owner-adjacent and narrative-adjacent: Papagal says it is sole-owned and managed by Matthew Maday, while Main Assembly calls The B Team its first investment, says The B Team is its incubation engine, and places Big Score, Taggable, The B Team and Neocurrency in the same project context. [Papagal; Main Assembly]

Prospective US and EU B2B buyers matter because the firm sells to companies across those markets, and the brief names founders, CTOs, VPs of engineering and product leaders as priority audiences. [The B Team site; Brief]

Referral sources and existing clients matter because Clutch reviews show referral-led sales and continuing engagements; public advocates include REAKT Agency, IT Broadcasting, True Productions, Taggable and Any All Every, with spend signals of about $100,000 for IT Broadcasting, about $140,000 for Taggable and about $1 million for True Productions. [Clutch]

Employees and future hires in Sofia matter through H512, DEV.BG, Joberty and YOX, but the talent record is thin and inconsistent: H512 and DEV.BG list tech stack and benefits, DEV.BG says no current jobs, YOX lists no opinions, and headcount ranges from 7 to 51-200 across sources. [H512; DEV.BG; Joberty; YOX; LinkedIn]

Regulators enter through claims, not enforcement: Bulgarian Registry Agency anchors company filings, Bulgaria’s data-protection authority matters for personal data, EU AI Act stakeholders matter because of AI, biometric and evaluation-tool claims, and Cyber Resilience Act authorities may matter if The B Team places software or hardware products on the EU market. [Registry Agency; CPDP; European Commission; The B Team site]

Still to check: named investor, lender, analyst, NGO or media stakeholders; Spain-address status; employee sentiment; client permissions; regulator comment; and independent corroboration for Third Party Pet and Microsoft Store case claims. [Banked gaps]

The context is an AI repositioning inside a mature export-software market: Bulgaria has about 10,000 ICT companies, 70% export-only, EUR 2.5 billion ICT revenue after 300% growth over seven years, and BASSCOM presents software as 87% export revenue with 11.5% growth. [U.S. Country Commercial Guide; BASSCOM]

AI demand is real but claim-risky: Gartner says only 17% of organizations have deployed AI agents while more than 60% expect to within two years, agentic AI is at the “Peak of Inflated Expectations,” and by 2027 40% of enterprises will demote or shut down autonomous agents because governance gaps emerge after incidents. [Gartner]

The EU AI Act entered into force on 1 August 2024, became generally applicable on 2 August 2026, and has literacy duties from 2 February 2025, GPAI obligations from 2 August 2025, and Article 50 transparency duties from 2 August 2026; biometric, interactive and generated-content claims therefore need careful disclosure discipline. [European Commission]

Data, security and product rules shape buyer checks: GDPR applies to SME personal-data processing, SCCs and the EU-US Data Privacy Framework matter for transatlantic transfers, DORA applies from 17 January 2025 to financial entities and their ICT-provider governance, the Cyber Resilience Act has reporting duties from 11 September 2026 and main obligations from 11 December 2027, and the new Product Liability Directive applies to EU-market products from 9 December 2026. [European Commission; EDPB]

Sustainability is not shown as a direct reporting duty for this small private firm, but CSRD supply-chain questions, SME taxonomy requests, AI energy scrutiny and green-claim rules make any responsible-AI or low-impact claim evidence-sensitive. [Brief; European Commission; EU Platform on Sustainable Finance; Microsoft]

Geopolitically, Sofia can be part of an EU AI-capability story through INSAIT, BgGPT, AI Factories, BRAIN++ and Bulgaria’s Digital Decade roadmap, but public sources do not connect The B Team to those programmes. [OECD; European Commission; CORDIS]

Still to check: direct NIS2, DORA, CRA, Accessibility Act, AI Act and product-liability status; data-processing roles, subprocessors, certifications, model-provider obligations, cloud regions, transfer mechanisms, continuity plans, AI-agent safety evidence and current AI case studies. [Banked gaps]

findings: Regulatory context. The B Team's own site claims Agentic AI Development, Workflow Automations and AI Company Upgrade services, so EU AI regulation is part of the operating context when work is placed on, used in, or affects people in the EU (https://thebteam.com/services; https://digital-strategy.ec.europa.eu/en/faqs/ai-literacy-questions-answers).

Regulatory context. The EU AI Act entered into force on 1 August 2024 and became generally applicable on 2 August 2026, while prohibited AI practices and AI literacy duties started on 2 February 2025 and general-purpose AI model obligations started on 2 August 2025 (https://digital-strategy.ec.europa.eu/en/policies/regulatory-framework-ai).

Regulatory context. The AI literacy duty applies to providers and deployers of AI systems, and Commission Q&A says Article 4 already applies from 2 February 2025 with supervision and enforcement rules applying from August 2026 (https://digital-strategy.ec.europa.eu/en/faqs/ai-literacy-questions-answers).

Regulatory context. AI Act Article 50 transparency duties apply from 2 August 2026 to certain generative and interactive AI systems and deepfakes, including duties to inform people when they interact directly with an AI system and to mark AI-generated or manipulated content (https://digital-strategy.ec.europa.eu/en/policies/guidelines-ai-transparency-obligations).

Regulatory context. document.hypothesis: The B Team's reputation problem is not weak capability; it is that the public proof system has not caught up with the AI-era story the company now wants buyers to believe. The white space is a proof-first AI software partner that shows exactly where its AI claim is true, where its public record still proves enterprise software craft better than AI depth, and where larger peers compete through scale and broader proof libraries. The strategy should first make the company easier to trust, then make it more visible. (rests on: AI proof gap) (rests on: Positioning-history pattern) (rests on: Each peer's share of voice) (rests on: Public identity pattern)

hypothesis_test.confirms: The hypothesis holds if client-approved proof shows shipped AI or automation work, named or anonymous but verifiable references, and a public proof library that connects the AI offer to existing enterprise software evidence.
hypothesis_test.overturns: The hypothesis is wrong if further research shows buyers already recognize The B Team as an AI specialist, the current AI claim is independently proven across recent work, and public inconsistency is not affecting trust or discovery.
